newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 12.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 12.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing,
Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
LONDON - Lingerie manufacturer Gossard, blasted by consumers last year for sexual imagery in its advertising, says it is launching a new poster campaign with "raunchy, humorous" headlines.

NEW YORK - D'Arcy, Masius, Benton & Bowles Communications has split its Asia-Pacific operations into two separate regions with presidents of each reporting to DMB&B chairman Arthur Selkowitz. DMB&B/Asia-Pacific North will comprise Hong Kong/China, Japan, Korea, Taiwan and the Philippines. The southern group includes Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia and New Zealand.

DUSSELDORF, Germany - German advertising agency TBWA Dusseldorf says its Frankfurt office has won the multi-million mark account for video game unit Sony Playstation. "With an eight-figure budget, several sale offers and consumer events, Sony and TBWA Frankfurt plan to develop the Playstation into a cult entertainment brand," says a TBWA spokeswoman.

PARIS - French oil, chemicals and healthcare company Elf Aquitaine is launching a press advertising campaign which seeks to give a human face to the firm, usually identified with the petrol pump. The account, with a budget of 30 million francs ($5.3 million), was won by advertising agency BDDP in competition with FCB, Euro RSCG, BETC and Publicis, an Elf spokeswoman says.

CHICAGO - Zenith Electronics Corp. is trying to put a bit of the old fire back into its brand image with a marketing and brand repositioning campaign featuring a new look, a concert tour promotion and a heavy autumn advertising lineup.

LOS ANGELES - Michael Jackson is coming out with a new album this month but it will be marketed in a much lower key way than previous albums, say industry experts. "In the last decade, the marketing of Jackson's product has always been bombastic," says Thomas White, an artists' rights expert.

MIAMI - Latin America has turned into a battleground for U.S. cable television networks vying against local rivals for viewers, according to the New York Times. Rising incomes, the introduction of satellite dishes and the proliferation of 24-hour news services have attracted cable television to Latin America, where a pay-television market is expected to generate at least $2.5 billion annually in advertising revenue and subscriber fees by 2000.
NEW YORK - Hungarian Broadcasting Corp says it expects an upward momentum in revenues to continue after the relaunch of its Budapest-based television station.

LONDON - Commercial radio continues to be Britain's fastest growing advertising medium, but the growth rate in 1996 was sharply below rates posted for the three previous years, the Radio Advertising Bureau says. Radio advertising revenues rose 14.0 percent to 308.8 million pounds in 1996, down from a growth rate of 22.9 percent in 1995, 23.4 percent in 1994 and 26.4 percent in 1993 it says.
LONDON - Britain's Daily Telegraph remained the country's top-selling broadsheet newspaper in April, despite a slight drop in circulation from March, the UK Audit Bureau of Circulation says.

REDWOOD CITY, California - Excite Inc. says it is set to launch a new online chat service that enables consumers to know whether friends, family or colleagues are online and to exchange messages with them.

LONDON - Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness Plc announce a merger worth more than 20 billion pounds ($32.5 billion) to create the world's seventh largest food and drinks company, GMG Brands. The merger will also form the world's leading branded spirits and wine company with combined spirits sales of over 100 million cases a year, bringing together brands such as GrandMet's Smirnoff vodka and Cinzano with Guinness-owned Johnnie Walker whisky and Gordon's gin.

NEW YORK - Ford Motor Co is considering joining with dealers in three U.S. cities to create auto superstores, the Wall Street Journal says. The venture will allow Ford, which now solely manufactures cars and trucks, to sell its vehicles directly to customers.

AMSTERDAM - Heineken reaches an agreement to become the worldwide preferred beer supplier to all Planet Hollywood restaurants outside the United States, the Dutch brewer says. Planet Hollywood International, owner and franchiser of the movie-themed restaurants with integrated merchandise outlets, currently has 58 Planet Hollywood locations worldwide, of which 33 are outside the U.S.

TURIN, Italy - The European new car market rose 9.2 percent to 1,258,200 units in April, says Italian vehicle makers association Anfia. New car registrations rose 1.3 percent in Germany, Britain was up 11.8 percent and Spain up 19.2 percent, while the fall in French sales continued, off 10 percent in April.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

NEW YORK - Upmarket jeweller Tiffany & Co sees sparkling prospects -- both domestically and internationally -- for its jewellery and other goods. Chairman William Chaney cites the strong economies in the U.S. and many other areas, especially the Asian Pacific Rim and Latin America, which are fuelling affluence and demand for high-priced items.

BEIJING - China is expected to see a rise in demand for bicycles in 1997 to 32 million but not from its own citizens but those overseas. The People's Daily Overseas Edition says export sales are climbing.
